{{technical|date=May 2025}}
In mathematical [[thermal conduction|heat conduction]], the '''Green's function number''' is used to uniquely categorize certain [[fundamental solution]]s of the [[heat equation]] to make existing solutions easier to identify, store, and retrieve.

Numbers have long been used to identify types of boundary conditions.<ref>{{harvnb|Luikov|1968}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Özışık |first1=M. Necati |title=Heat conduction |date=1980 |publisher=Wiley |location=New York |isbn=047105481X |edition=1st}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Nowak |first1=A. |last2=Białecki |first2=R. |last3=Kurpisz |first3=K. |title=Evaluating eigenvalues for boundary value problems of heat conduction in rectangular and cylindrical co-ordinate systems |journal=International Journal for Numerical Methods in Engineering |date=February 1987 |volume=24 |issue=2 |pages=419–445 |doi=10.1002/nme.1620240210|bibcode=1987IJNME..24..419N }}</ref> The Green's function number system was proposed by Beck and Litkouhi in 1988<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Beck |first1=James V. |last2=Litkouhi |first2=Bahman |title=Heat conduction numbering system for basic geometries |journal=International Journal of Heat and Mass Transfer |date=March 1988 |volume=31 |issue=3 |pages=505–515 |doi=10.1016/0017-9310(88)90032-4}}</ref> and has seen increasing use since then.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Al-Nimr |first1=M. A. |last2=Alkam |first2=M. K. |title=A generalized thermal boundary condition |journal=Heat and Mass Transfer |date=19 September 1997 |volume=33 |issue=1–2 |pages=157–161 |doi=10.1007/s002310050173|bibcode=1997HMT....33..157A |s2cid=119549322 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=de Monte |first1=Filippo |title=Multi-layer transient heat conduction using transition time scales |journal=International Journal of Thermal Sciences |date=September 2006 |volume=45 |issue=9 |pages=882–892 |doi=10.1016/j.ijthermalsci.2005.11.006|bibcode=2006IJTS...45..882D }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Lefebvre |first1=G. |title=A general modal-based numerical simulation of transient heat conduction in a one-dimensional homogeneous slab |journal=Energy and Buildings |date=December 2010 |volume=42 |issue=12 |pages=2309–2322 |doi=10.1016/j.enbuild.2010.07.024|bibcode=2010EneBu..42.2309L }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | title = Construction of a code verification matrix for heat conduction with finite element code applications | author1= Toptan, A. | author2 = Porter, N. W.| author3 = Hales, J. D.  | journal = Journal of Verification, Validation and Uncertainty Quantification | volume = 5 | issue = 4 | pages = 041002 | year = 2020 | doi= 10.1115/1.4049037 | doi-access = | osti= 2352626 }}</ref> The number system has been used to catalog a large collection of Green's functions and related solutions.<ref>{{harvnb|Cole|Beck|Haji-Sheikh|Litkouhi|2011}}</ref><ref name="GFLib">{{cite web | url = https://www.engr.unl.edu/~glibrary/home/index.html | title = Green's Function Library | access-date = November 19, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url= http://exact.unl.edu/ | title= Exact Analytical Conduction Toolbox|access-date= March 4, 2021}}</ref>

Although the examples given below are for the [[heat equation]], this number system applies to any phenomena described by [[differential equation]]s such as [[diffusion]], [[acoustics]], [[electromagnetics]], [[fluid dynamics]], etc.

==Notation==
The Green's function number specifies the [[coordinate system]] and the type of [[boundary condition]]s that a [[Green's function]] satisfies. The Green's function number has two parts, a letter designation followed by a number designation.  The letter(s) designate the coordinate system, while the numbers designate the type of boundary conditions that are satisfied.

{| class="wikitable" style="text-align: center"
|+ Table 1.  Boundary conditions designations for Green's function number system. 
|-
! Name                   !! Boundary condition !! Number   
|-
| No physical boundary   || G is bounded                                    || 0
|-
| Dirichlet              || <math> G =  0 </math>                           || 1
|-
| Neumann                || <math> \frac{\partial G}{\partial n} = 0 </math>       || 2 
|-
| Robin                  || <math> k \frac{\partial G}{\partial n} + h G= 0</math> || 3
|}

Some of the designations for the Greens function number system are given next. Coordinate system designations include:  X, Y, and Z for Cartesian coordinates; R, Z, φ for [[Cylindrical coordinate system|cylindrical coordinates]]; and, RS, φ, θ for spherical coordinates. 
Designations for several boundary conditions are given in Table 1. The zeroth boundary condition is important for identifying the presence of a coordinate boundary where no physical boundary exists, for example, far away in a semi-infinite body or at the center of a cylindrical or spherical body.

== Examples in Cartesian coordinates ==

=== X11 ===
As an example, number X11 denotes the Green's function that satisfies the heat equation in the domain ({{math|0 < ''x'' < ''L''}}) for boundary conditions of type 1 ([[Dirichlet boundary condition|Dirichlet]]) at both boundaries {{math|1=''x'' = 0}} and {{math|1=''x'' = ''L''}}.  Here '''X''' denotes the Cartesian coordinate and '''11''' denotes the type 1 boundary condition at both sides of the body. The [[boundary value problem]] for the X11 Green's function is given by

{| class="wikitable" style="margin-left:1.5em;"
! scope="row" | Equation
| <math>\frac{\partial^2 G}{\partial x^2} + \frac{1}{\alpha} \delta(t - \tau) \delta(x - x') = \frac{1}{\alpha} \frac{\partial G}{\partial t}</math>
|-
! scope="row" | Domain
| {{plainlist|
* <math>0 < x < L</math>
* <math>t > 0</math>
}}
|-
! scope="row" | Boundary conditions
| {{plainlist|
* <math>G(x=0) = 0</math>, <math>G(x=L) = 0</math>
* <math>G(t<\tau) = 0</math>
}}
|}
Here <math> \alpha </math> is the [[thermal diffusivity]] (m<sup>2</sup>/s) and <math> \delta </math> is the [[Dirac delta function]].
This GF is developed elsewhere.<ref>{{harvnb|Luikov|1968|p=388}}</ref><ref>{{harvnb|Cole|Beck|Haji-Sheikh|Litkouhi|2011}}</ref>

=== X20 ===
As another Cartesian example, number X20 denotes the Green's function in the semi-infinite body (<math>0<x<\infty </math>) with a Neumann (type 2) boundary at {{math|1=''x'' = 0}}.  Here '''X''' denotes the Cartesian coordinate, '''2''' denotes the type 2 boundary condition at {{math|1=''x'' = 0}} and '''0''' denotes the zeroth type boundary condition (boundedness) at <math>  x = \infty </math>. The [[boundary value problem]] for the X20 Green's function is given by
{| class="wikitable" style="margin-left:1.5em;"
! scope="row" | Equation
| <math>\frac{\partial^2 G}{\partial x^2} +\frac{1}{\alpha} \delta(t - \tau) \delta(x - x') = \frac{1}{\alpha} \frac{\partial G}{\partial t}</math>
|-
! scope="row" | Domain
| {{plainlist|
* <math>0 < x < \infty</math>
* <math>t > 0</math>
}}
|-
! scope="row" | Boundary conditions
| {{plainlist|
* <math>\left.\frac{\partial G}{\partial n} \right|_{x=0}=0</math>, <math>\left.G \right|_{x\to \infty}</math> is bounded,
* <math>G(t<\tau) = 0</math>
}}
|}
This GF is published elsewhere.<ref>{{harvnb|Luikov|1968|p=387}}</ref><ref>{{harvnb|Carslaw|Jaeger|1959|p=276}}</ref>

=== X10Y20 ===
As a two-dimensional example, number X10Y20 denotes the Green's function in the quarter-infinite body (<math>0<x<\infty </math>, <math>0<y<\infty </math>) with a Dirichlet (type 1) boundary at {{math|1=''x'' = 0}} and a Neumann (type 2) boundary at {{math|1=''y'' = 0}}.  The [[boundary value problem]] for the X10Y20 Green's function is given by
{| class="wikitable" style="margin-left:1.5em;"
! scope="row" | Equation
| <math>\frac{\partial^2 G}{\partial x^2} +\frac{\partial^2 G}{\partial y^2} + \frac{1}{\alpha} \delta(t - \tau) \delta(x - x')  \delta(y - y') = \frac{1}{\alpha} \frac{\partial G}{\partial t}</math>
|-
! scope="row" | Domain
|  {{plainlist|
* <math>0 < x < \infty</math>
* <math>0 < y < \infty</math>
* <math>t > 0</math>
}}
|-
! scope="row" | Boundary conditions
| {{plainlist|
* <math>G(x=0) = 0</math>, <math>\left.G \right|_{x\to \infty}</math> is bounded,
* <math>\left.\frac{\partial G}{\partial n} \right|_{y=0}=0</math>, <math>G |_{y\to \infty}</math> is bounded,
* <math>G(t<\tau) = 0</math>
}}
|}
Applications of related half-space and quarter-space GF are available.<ref>{{cite journal | title =Conduction in rectangular plates with boundary temperatures specified | last1 = Beck | first1 = J. V. | last2 = Wright | first2 = N. | last3 = Haji-Sheikh | first3 = A. | last4 = Cole | first4 = K. D | author5 = Amos. D. | journal = International Journal of Heat and Mass Transfer | volume = 52 | issue = 19–20 | pages = 4676–4690 | year = 2008 | doi= 10.1016/j.ijheatmasstransfer.2008.02.020 | bibcode = 2008IJHMT..51.4676B | s2cid = 12677235 | url = https://digitalcommons.unl.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=1036&context=mechengfacpub | url-access = subscription }}</ref>

== Examples in cylindrical coordinates ==

=== R03 ===
As an example in the cylindrical coordinate system, number R03 denotes the Green's function that satisfies the heat equation in the solid cylinder ({{math|0 < ''r'' < ''a''}}) with a boundary condition of type 3 (Robin) at {{math|1=''r'' = ''a''}}.  Here letter '''R''' denotes the cylindrical coordinate system, number '''0''' denotes the zeroth boundary condition (boundedness) at the center of the cylinder ({{math|1=''r'' = 0}}), and number '''3''' denotes the type 3 ([[Robin boundary condition|Robin]]) boundary condition at {{math|1=''r'' = ''a''}}. The boundary value problem for R03 Green's function is given by
{| class="wikitable" style="margin-left:1.5em;"
! scope="row" | Equation
| <math>\frac{1}{r} \frac{\partial}{\partial r} \left( r \frac{\partial G}{\partial r} \right) + \frac{1}{\alpha} \delta(t - \tau) \frac{\delta(r - r')}{2 \pi r'} = \frac{1}{\alpha} \frac{\partial G}{\partial t}</math>
|-
! scope="row" | Domain
| {{plainlist|
* <math>0 < r < a</math>
* <math>t > 0</math>
}}
|-
! scope="row" | Boundary conditions
| {{plainlist|
* <math>G(r=0)</math> is bounded, <math>\left. k \frac{\partial G}{\partial n} \right|_{r=a} + \left. h G \right|_{r=a} =0</math>,
* <math>G(t<\tau) = 0</math>
}}
|}
Here <math> k </math> is [[thermal conductivity]] (W/(m K)) and <math> h </math> is the [[heat transfer coefficient]] (W/(m<sup>2</sup> K)).
See {{harvtxt|Carslaw|Jaeger|1959|p=369}}, {{harvtxt|Cole|Beck|Haji-Sheikh|Litkouhi|2011|p=543}} for this GF.

=== R10 ===
As another example, number R10 denotes the Green's function in a large body containing a cylindrical void (a < r < <math> \infty </math>) with a type 1 (Dirichlet) boundary condition at {{math|1=''r'' = ''a''}}.  Again letter '''R''' denotes the cylindrical coordinate system, number '''1''' denotes the type 1 boundary at {{math|1=''r'' = ''a''}}, and number '''0''' denotes the type zero boundary (boundedness) at large values of r. The boundary value problem for the R10 Green's function is given by
{| class="wikitable" style="margin-left:1.5em;"
! scope="row" | Equation
| <math>\frac{1}{r} \frac{\partial}{\partial r} \left( r \frac{\partial G}{\partial r} \right) + \frac{1}{\alpha} \delta(t - \tau) \frac{\delta(r - r')}{2 \pi r'} = \frac{1}{\alpha} \frac{\partial G}{\partial t}</math>
|-
! scope="row" | Domain
| {{plainlist|
* <math>a < r < \infty</math>
* <math>t > 0</math>
}}
|-
! scope="row" | Boundary conditions
| {{plainlist|
* <math>G(r=a) = 0</math>, <math>G |_{r\to \infty}</math> is bounded,
* <math>G(t<\tau) = 0</math>
}}
|}
This GF is available elsewhere. <ref>{{harvnb|Carslaw|Jaeger|1959|p=378}}</ref><ref>{{cite book | last = Thambynayagam | first = R. K. M. | title = The Diffusion Handbook | publisher = McGraw-Hill | date = 2011 | page = 432 | isbn = 9780071751841}}</ref>

=== R01φ00 ===
As a two dimensional example, number R01φ00 denotes the Green's function in a solid cylinder with angular dependence, with a type 1 (Dirichlet) boundary condition at {{math|1=''r'' = a}}. Here letter '''φ''' denotes the angular (azimuthal) coordinate, and numbers '''00''' denote the type zero boundaries for angle; here no physical boundary takes the form of the periodic boundary condition.  The boundary value problem for the R01φ00 Green's function is given by
{| class="wikitable" style="margin-left:1.5em;"
! scope="row" | Equation
| <math>\frac{1}{r}\frac{\partial}{\partial r} \left( r \frac{\partial G}{\partial r} \right) + \frac{1}{r^2}\frac{\partial^2 G}{\partial \phi^2} + \frac{1}{\alpha} \delta(t - \tau) \frac{\delta(r - r')}{2 \pi r'}  \delta(\phi - \phi ') = \frac{1}{\alpha} \frac{\partial G}{\partial t}</math>
|-
! scope="row" | Domain
| {{plainlist|
* <math>0 < r < a</math>
* <math>0 < \phi < 2\pi</math>
* <math>t > 0</math>
}}
|-
! scope="row" | Boundary conditions
|{{plainlist|
* <math>G(r=0)</math> is bounded, <math>G(r=a) = 0</math>,
* <math>G(\phi=0) = G(\phi=2\pi)</math>, <math>\left.\frac{\partial G}{\partial \phi}\right|_{\phi=0} = \left.\frac{\partial G}{\partial \phi} \right|_{\phi=2 \pi}</math>
* <math>G(t<\tau) = 0</math>
}}
|}
Both a transient<ref>{{harvnb|Cole|Beck|Haji-Sheikh|Litkouhi|2011|p=554}}</ref> and steady form<ref>{{cite book | last = Melnikov | first = Y. A. | title = Influence Functions and Matrices | publisher = Marcel Dekker | location = New York | date = 1999 | page = 223 | isbn = 9780824719418 }}</ref> of this GF are available.

== Example in spherical coordinates ==
=== RS02 ===
As an example in the [[spherical coordinate system]], number RS02 denotes the Green's function for a solid sphere ({{math|0 < ''r'' < ''b''}}) with a type 2 ([[Neumann boundary condition|Neumann]]) boundary condition at {{math|1=''r'' = ''b''}}.  Here letters '''RS''' denote the radial-spherical coordinate system, number '''0''' denotes the zeroth boundary condition (boundedness) at {{math|1=''r'' = 0}}, and number '''2''' denotes the type 2 boundary at {{math|1=''r'' = ''b''}}.  The boundary value problem for the RS02 Green's function is given by
{| class="wikitable" style="margin-left:1.5em;"
! scope="row" | Equation
| <math>\frac{1}{r^2}\frac{\partial}{\partial r} \left( r^2 \frac{\partial G}{\partial r} \right) + \frac{1}{\alpha} \delta(t -  \tau) \frac{\delta(r - r')}{4 \pi r^2} = \frac{1}{\alpha} \frac{\partial G}{\partial t}</math>
|-
! scope="row" | Domain
| {{plainlist|
* <math>0 < r < b</math>
* <math>t > 0</math>
}}
|-
! scope="row" | Boundary conditions
| {{plainlist|
* <math>G(r=0)</math> is bounded, <math>\left.\frac{\partial G}{\partial n} \right|_{r=a} = 0</math>,
* <math>G(t<\tau) = 0</math>
}}
|}
This GF is available elsewhere.<ref>{{harvnb|Cole|Beck|Haji-Sheikh|Litkouhi|2011|p=309}}</ref>
